title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-07-28
content:
Attendees: Priya (notes), Ethan, Zoe, Marcus, Anna (brief check-in)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Quantization: QA run for 4-bit INT4 kernels completed on RQ-1 model family; tail latency regressions observed on long-context (>= 4096) sequences. Follow-ups: measure KV-cache memory lanes and adjust kernel tiling.
- Evals: New open-source benchmark harness integrated into CI; initial regression detected for A/B rollout between v2026-07-15 and v2026-07-22 on toxic-span recall. Rolling back canary for affected customer routes.
- Model onboarding: RQ-1.1 successful on Dedicated staging with 2x throughput improvement w/ q4_0; need to validate output fidelity vs golden set.
- Action items: prioritize kernel tiling change (Ethan), expand eval prompt sets for code generation and toxicity (Zoe), create customer-impact matrix for rollout (Marcus).

Notes by section:

1) Quantization experiments
- What we ran this week:
  - Batch of int4 experiments on RQ-1 and RQ-1.1 using q4_0 and q4_k_m optimized kernels on NVIDIA H100 and A100.
  - Config: sequence lengths 512/2048/4096, batch sizes 1/4/8, kv-cache warm/cold.
- Results (high level):
  - Latency: p50 reduced ~30-45% vs fp16 for 512/2048 sequences on both HW types.
  - Tail latency: for sequences >= 4096 we see p95/p99 increases of ~15-40% on H100 when using q4_0 kernel vs fp16 baseline. More pronounced when batch size >1.
  - Memory: peak GPU memory reduced ~2.2x enabling +2 in max concurrent requests per GPU.
  - Quality: Perplexity delta small (<0.6) on standard corpora but we observed slight tokenization mismatch in a handful of German/compound-word cases.
- Hypothesis on tail latency regression:
  - Kernel tiling and KV-cache eviction strategy cause extra synchronization when sequence length crosses internal tile boundary. Also branch in attention routine triggers slower path for long sequences.
- Experiment next week:
  - Ethan to implement a tiling-alignment micropatch to try to avoid cross-tile synchronization. Run with synthetic long-seq workloads (8k, 12k) to stress. Target: p99 <= +10% over fp16.
  - Marcus to validate q4_k_m fallback codepath on Dedicated nodes to ensure API behavior identical when kernel selection changes.

2) Evals and regression detection
- CI integration:
  - Zoe finished hooking the open-benchmark harness into the nightly CI (runs on a small hosted instance). It will produce a metrics diff and highlight regressions for toxicity, instruction-following, and code-gen.
- Findings this week:
  - Canary rollout comparison (v2026-07-15 -> v2026-07-22) showed a delta in toxic-span recall for conversational prompts (up ~6% false positives). Tracked to slight token output distribution shift under q4_0 for a minority of prompts.
  - Code-gen: no large performance or correctness deltas on top-1; however BLEU and exact-match microdrops observed on longer functions (>80 tokens).
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Rolled back canary for customer route: customer-alpha (sensitive jurisdiction). Notified CS + Solutions.
- Next steps:
  - Expand eval prompt sets to include more long-form code and multi-turn dialog contexts. Zoe to add 120 new prompts pulled from GH issues and customer repros.
  - Add metric: token-level KL and distribution drift to complement perplexity.

3) Model onboarding status (RQ-1.1, FLAN variants)
- RQ-1.1 (maintained by Applied ML):
  - Staging Dedicated: onboarded and performance validated for q4_0 quantized profile. Throughput +2x reported in load tests.
  - Fidelity tests: 1000-sample golden set run shows 98.7% match threshold (we set 99.5 target) - failing cases concentrated on hallucination-likely prompts and rare named-entity boundaries.
  - Action: run targeted re-eval with alternative tokenizers and adjust post-processing normalizers. Priya to own coordination with tokenizer team.
- FLAN-Tiny/FLAN-XL intake:
  - FLAN-Tiny: quick smoke pass OK. Candidate for low-latency hosted routes.
  - FLAN-XL: initial on-prem packaging done; still hitting OOM on smallest Dedicated SKU with fp16; quantization path in progress.

4) Production/Deployment notes
- Smart routing/fallbacks: Identified a gap where q4_k_m fallback to fp16 was not being surfaced to the autoscaler metrics - this caused misleading per-GPU utilization when models hit fallback path. Marcus to add metric labels by kernel.
- Canary / rollout cadence: propose we shorten canary window from 48h -> 24h for low-risk patches (e.g., kernel scheduling) and keep 72h for model changes. Discuss in Release Eng sync.
- Observability: add token-level cost breakdown for quantized runs to Console (ask: SRE/Console teams). Logged in INF-327.

5) Blockers & Risks
- Blocker: kernel tiling fix is non-trivial and affects several optimized kernels - risk to throughput if patched incorrectly. Need isolated perf harness and QA gating.
- Risk: fidelity target for RQ-1.1 not yet met; could delay Dedicated customer onboarding by 1 sprint if not resolved.
- Mitigation: fallbacks and canary rollbacks are in place; expand golden set and include customer-specific tests earlier in onboarding.

6) Action items (owner + due)
- Ethan: implement tiling-alignment patch, run perf harness across H100/A100, share results by 2026-08-03.
- Zoe: add 120 eval prompts (toxicity + code long-form), integrate token-KL drift metric in nightly CI, deadline 2026-08-05.
- Marcus: add kernel-labels to autoscaler metrics and validate fallback accounting; PR by 2026-08-04.
- Priya: coordinate tokenizer re-eval for RQ-1.1, run targeted golden set + normalized comparisons, update by 2026-08-06.
- Anna (CS): prepare customer-impact summary for customer-alpha and schedule review call with legal.

Meeting notes / miscellaneous:
- Quick sync with Release Eng: agreed to add a small boolean flag in rollout config to disable quantization kernels per-route for emergency rollbacks. Release Eng to scope.
- Observability ask: Console team requested example payloads and metric names; Zoe will provide sample output from harness.
- FYI: benchmarks folder (internal) has new long-seq synthetic traces: s3://redwood-bench/longseq/2026-07-26/ - use for stress runs.

Ideas / backlog items (brainstorm):
- Investigate adaptive quantization: dynamic per-layer precision based on activation variance at runtime. Longer-term R&D, could save additional memory.
- Prompt-aware caching: detect long-reuse prefix across sessions and pin in KV cache to reduce cold-start for multi-turn flows.
- Customer-guides: write short note on "how to interpret quantized-performance in Console" for Solutions engineers.

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (nightly run 2026-07-28)
- RQ-1 int4 (q4_0) vs fp16 (seq=2048, batch=1): p50 -35%, p95 -12%, p99 +9%
- Memory reduction: ~2.2x
- Throughput (servers per 8-GPU pod): fp16=320 tokens/s, q4_0=670 tokens/s (approx)

References / links:
- Confluence: quantization playbook (linked above)
- GitHub PR: serving-runtime #842 (tiling WIP)
- Jira: APPLIED-512 (RQ-1.1 onboarding), INF-327 (observability quantized metrics)

Notes to self: keep the weekly note short next week and surface only customer-impacting deltas.

End of notes.
